Messages.Author: James B. Floate
Messages.Body:
Me again,

You can fortitude off the damage from Rutor's Hand at Super, can you
Skin of Night it into normal damage?
If this is the case then the 'can prevent' clause on Rutor's Hand means
a more general 'may react to the damage'. I love the idea of wrapping
your hand in a flak jacket and cutting it off, and saying 'Gee, that
didnt hurt as much as I thought it would'.

Thanks,
James.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
James B. Floate wrote:
>
> Me again,
>
> You can fortitude off the damage from Rutor's Hand at Super, can you
> Skin of Night it into normal damage?

Yes.

> If this is the case then the 'can prevent' clause on Rutor's Hand means
> a more general 'may react to the damage'.

Not exactly. The 'can prevent' clause inspired the Rules Team
to issue the errata that the damage (from superior Rutor's Hand) is
treated as if from a strike in combat. This errata leads to the
ability to play combat cards like Skin of Night.

> I love the idea of wrapping
> your hand in a flak jacket and cutting it off, and saying 'Gee, that
> didnt hurt as much as I thought it would'.

Yeah, the card combos can look pretty silly sometimes.

--

The only way to prevent this damage (that I know of) is using Blood Tears.
Everything else is specific to combat and you are NOT in combat when you
take this damage.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
bra...@acsu.buffalo.edu wrote:
> On Tue, 15 Apr 1997, James B. Floate wrote:

> > [...] the damage from Rutor's Hand at Super [...]

> The only way to prevent this damage (that I know of) is using Blood Tears.
> Everything else is specific to combat and you are NOT in combat when you
> take this damage.

Rutor's Hand superior has errata that the damage is treated as if from
a strike in combat. So combat effects are allowed (Skin of Rock, Flak
Jacket, superior Sideslip, etc.).
